{{nihongo|'''Asukabe Shrine'''|飛鳥戸神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Asukabe Shrine''' (あすかべじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Asuka, {{ill|Habikino|Q694308|qid=Q694308}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined Deity ===
At present, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined. This is because during the Edo period {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}} was the enshrined deity, and at the time of {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} it was changed to Susanoo-no-Mikoto.

This area was the place of residence of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Asukabe no Miyatsuko}} clan, descendants of {{ill|Paekche|Q28428|qid=Q28428}} royalty—specifically the descendants of {{ill|Buyeo Gonji|Q6790050|qid=Q6790050|lt=King Gonji}}—who were dispatched and came to Japan in the {{ill|5th century|Q8095|qid=Q8095}}. It is thought that originally King Gonji was enshrined as the ancestral deity of the Asukabe no Miyatsuko. In the Baekje Annals of the 『{{ill|Samguk sagi|Q485552|qid=Q485552}}』 it is recorded that King Gonji died in Baekje at the beginning of the Ungjin period; even if Gonji himself returned home, it is thought that his descendants remained in Japan. Nearby, the Shingū Kofun Cluster ({{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|ko|굴식 돌방무덤|zh|橫穴式石室|qid=Q11543435}}) is said by one theory to be the burial ground of the Asuka clan.

In 『Kawachi no Kuni Shikigami Shikō』 it is recorded as “Prince Yasuyado,” in 『Draft Manuscript of the Register of Shikinaisha in Kawachi Province』 as “Ancestral deity of the Baekje clan, commonly called {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunabikona-no-Mikoto}},” and in 『Jinja Yōroku』 as “Ancestral deity of the Baekje clan, name unknown.”

On the other hand, {{ill|Saeki Ariyoshi|Q13364959|qid=Q13364959}} states that in 『{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}』, volume 24 (Ukyō Shoban) and volume 28 (Kawachi no Kuni Shoban), it is written: “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Asukabe no Miyatsuko}}. Son of King Biu of Baekje, descended from {{ill|Buyeo Gonji|Q6790050|qid=Q6790050|lt=King Gonji}}.”<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book|author={{ill|Saeki Ariyoshi|Q13364959|qid=Q13364959}}|date=1998-09-01|title=Studies on the Shinsen Shōjiroku|series=Textual Criticism Volume 5|publisher={{ill|Yoshikawa Kōbunkan|Q4346755|qid=Q4346755}}|ISBN=4642021159|page=2}}</ref>

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown.

The first appearance in official histories is an entry dated August 13 of the first year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) in 『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}』, stating that the shrine was granted the divine rank of Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is listed as “Asukabe Shrine, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasuka District}}, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}},” and is ranked as a Myōjin Taisha. Until the Edo period, there was a {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} (shrine-temple) called {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jōrin-ji}}, founded by {{ill|Gyōki|Q1136664|qid=Q1136664}}, and it was designated a {{ill|Chokugansho|Q22131160|qid=Q22131160}} of {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}}.

In the early Meiji period it was ranked as a Village Shrine, but in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 41 ({{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}) it was {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=merged}} with a nearby Hachiman Shrine (now {{ill|Tsuboi Hachimangū|Q11429677|qid=Q11429677}}). In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 27 ({{ill|1952|Q5272|qid=Q5272}}) it was separated and rebuilt near the former shrine site.
